title: 'Loudcasters' on English Buses to Face Fines
paragraphs: Public transport passengers in England will soon have to think again if they want to listen to music or watch videos without headphones.
Local authorities across the country now have the power to bring in stricter rules against this so-called "loudcasting" on public buses, which has become a common annoyance.

One survey found that eight in 10 British people find loudcasting annoying — though 46% admitted to watching videos without headphones in public places sometimes themselves, and 36% said they listened to music without headphones.
The new rules mean that local authorities can fine passengers playing loud music or videos on their phones up to about $130.
Loudcasting isn't the only bad behavior that local authorities have gotten more power to fight against either, as they can now also fine people for things like vaping and littering on buses.
Bus drivers won't be the ones enforcing these rules though, as this job will instead be done by trained transport safety officers and the police.
The rules against loudcasting are getting stricter on trains too, where there had already been laws against playing music since 2005.
Now, if someone is asked to turn down the noise by railway staff and they don't do it, they will have to leave at the next station or pay up to about $1,300.

Many different train operators already have their own campaigns telling passengers how they should behave. However, the government has also announced a shared campaign to inform people about the new rules and tell them to "share the carriage, not the noise."
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, "We've all been on the train when someone starts blasting music or videos from their phone. It gets on your nerves and can quickly spoil the journey."
He added that creating stricter rules is "a simple thing, but one that will make journeys that little bit better for all of us."
